teams.heading: Jake White opens Fiji reign with 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo
teams.body: Ben Volavola's two second-half penalties settled a 34-28 win over Japan in Tokyo, Jake White's first match in charge of Fiji. Japan and Fiji each scored three first-half tries, and Fiji were briefly down to 14 when Motikai Murray was yellow-carded, a card later upgraded to red. The win avenges September's 20-15 Pacific Nations Cup final defeat to Japan, and Fiji's November Nations Championship tour takes them to France, Ireland and Italy.

lead.why: It is a new men's Test result for Fiji, the first match of Jake White's tenure, and it is not covered in the already-reported stories.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby tips Barton, Jibulu and Hicks as England call-up options
teams.body: Planet Rugby has put forward seven uncapped players as options for England's November Tests, and three are George Barton, Nathan Jibulu and Max Hicks. Gloucester full-back Barton is in strong form and automatic off the tee, while Sale hooker Jibulu, 23, has won two man-of-the-match awards this season. Hicks, a New Zealand-born back-rower in his first Premiership season at Newcastle, qualifies through ancestry. Australia, Japan and the All Blacks are pencilled in for November, and Jamie George is nearing the end of his Test career.

lead.why: A new national-team selection item for England's November Tests, which the other candidates either repeat (Randall) or are not men's England stories (Red Roses, club transfers).

teams.heading: Galthié names uncapped Jeremy Ward, drops Nicolas Depoortere from France squad
teams.body: Fabien Galthié has dropped Bordeaux's Nicolas Depoortere to create a place for Jeremy Ward, a former Junior Springboks captain, in the November squad, Planet Rugby reports. The South African-born Ward is not eligible for France until next year, so Planet Rugby describes his inclusion as purely for training purposes. Galthié is making the change amid a growing injury list, and Ward is one of several uncapped players in a 42-man squad that faces Fiji, South Africa and Argentina.

lead.why: The Ward and Depoortere selections are a separate France squad storyline from the Alldritt recall already covered, and the pack carries no fresh Test-side item that is new.

teams.heading: Farrell names uncapped James McNabney and Jamie Benson; Conan ruled out
teams.body: Andy Farrell has given uncapped Ulster pair James McNabney and Jamie Benson their first Ireland squad places, with Jack Conan ruled out by a shoulder injury. McNabney is back from an ACL injury that cost him all of 2025/26, while Benson has played between centre and out-half for Ulster this season. Farrell on McNabney: "He's some specimen of a man and he certainly runs his weight." Harry Byrne, Jack Crowley, Caelan Doris and Bryn Ward also miss out through injury, RTÉ Sport reports.

lead.why: A fresh Ireland squad story with two uncapped debutants and a key injury absence, distinct from the captaincy item already run on 22 October.

teams.heading: Italy lost 32-14 to South Africa at home in November 2025
teams.body: Italy lost 32-14 at home to South Africa in November 2025, in an International Friendly, and South Africa are Italy's next opponent. In the log, Italy sit 11 of 12 after three games, with no wins from those three. Across those three games, Italy have scored 37 points and conceded 131, a points difference of -94 over those games.

teams.heading: Scotland's unprecedented squad depth could force multiple big-name omissions ahead of November
teams.body: The Scotsman reports that Scotland's unprecedented depth could lead to several big names being left out of the Nations Championship squad. Depth is the theme elsewhere too: BBC Sport's Tom English says Rory Darge's consistency leaves Freddy Douglas scrapping for a bench place, while Dobie, Steyn and Rowe jostle for the wing spots. Jack Dempsey is also available for the Nations Championship.

teams.heading: Taulupe Faletau to have finger surgery after Cardiff comeback, misses Ospreys derby
teams.body: BBC Sport reports Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau will have surgery on a finger injury picked up on his Cardiff comeback, ruling him out of the URC derby at Ospreys. The 35-year-old made his first appearance since March in the Champions Cup defeat by Northampton. Van Zyl said Faletau would be on the sidelines "for a while", adding: "hopefully after November he will be fine." Faletau, who has 109 caps, was left out of Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad, and Tandy wants him to show durability.

lead.why: A new injury to a senior Wales men's international is the only fresh men's Test-side item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards signs as Argentina defence coach through 2027 World Cup
teams.body: Shaun Edwards has signed on as Argentina's defence coach until the end of the 2027 World Cup, he told Rugby World. Argentina were the first team to offer him a contract, and England's men's boss had told him they were happy with their own staff. "I want to go to the World Cup," Edwards said. He pointed to France's group-stage defence at the last World Cup, conceding an average of 12 points a game, as the standard he wants to match.

lead.why: It is the only item in today's pack that is new to readers and concerns Argentina's own coaching staff.

teams.heading: Pierre Brousset to referee Wallabies' England Test in Nations Championship
teams.body: World Rugby has named Pierre Brousset to referee England v Australia in the Nations Championship, with Nika Amashukeli and Jeremy Rozier as assistants. The appointment comes weeks after Michael Hooper criticised referee Andrea Piardi following the Springboks' 42-38 defeat to the Wallabies in September, when Australia had only 11 players on the field at one stage after four quick-fire sin-binnings. Piardi is now assigned to France v Springboks in round two.

lead.why: It is a new national Test item on the Wallabies' England fixture, and it links to the Piardi row that Michael Hooper raised.

teams.heading: Cheslin Kolbe returns to Stormers after Suntory spell, missing family in Japan
teams.body: Springbok winger Cheslin Kolbe has left Japanese club Suntory Sungoliath, who he joined after the 2023 World Cup, to return to the Stormers. His final stint in Japan was the most challenging, with his wife and children staying in South Africa during the season. "I've been wanting to come home for so long," Kolbe told the For the Love of Rugby podcast, adding: "I don't regret anything at all." His Stormers debut was delayed after he broke his jaw on international duty.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen calls World Rugby a 'secret society' over yellow cards
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Sir Steve Hansen has accused World Rugby of being a "secret society", arguing the governing body does not tell fans enough about officiating decisions. Speaking on the Rugby Unity podcast, as Planet Rugby reports, Hansen said the yellow card "needs urgent work", pointing to games where sides are reduced for offences he says are unintentional. He expects the November summit of coaches and referees to talk about how the November Tests will be refereed, and wants the TMO questions answered.

lead.why: It is the only new union item that isn't a squad or injury story already run, or a league story.

teams.heading: Springbok Andre Esterhuizen forced off with foot injury in Sharks' Cardiff match
teams.body: Sharks captain Andre Esterhuizen was forced off with a foot injury after just 52 seconds of Friday's URC match at Cardiff, landing awkwardly on his right foot after an aerial duel and unable to stand on it, with Jaco Williams coming on. Planet Rugby reports Rassie Erasmus is expected to name his Nations Championship squad in the upcoming week, and no update on the injury's severity has been published.

lead.why: A current Springbok injury ahead of the Nations Championship squad announcement is fresher national-team news than the Kolbe feature already run.
